Lesson 6 · Technical continuation

Which stores will need attention next week?

The same stores, calculation, and decision—with the specification and reproducible steps visible.

Baseline only · targets in weeks 3–16 · no alerts yet

← Return to the worked analysis

Use the same analysis rows

Training, validation, and test windows refer to target weeks. A row predicting week t uses lag_rate from t−1 and planned variables for t. The train/validation split chooses the model class; the final test evaluates the selected class after refitting on weeks 3–13.

Case seed: 20261109. All ten labs use the same store IDs and underlying records. Read the shared data dictionary.

Reproduce the calculation

The candidates are ordinary least squares and a tree limited to depth three with at least 30 training rows per leaf. No missing-value imputation is needed in the reconciled forecast view. Model restrictions are set before inspecting the final period.

data = world()['panel'].query('3 <= week <= 16')
features = ['lag_rate','lead_days','urban','demand_forecast','promotion_plan']
train = data.query('week <= 10')
valid = data.query('11 <= week <= 13')
test = data.query('week >= 14')
models = {'Linear regression': LinearRegression(),
          'Small tree': DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=3,min_samples_leaf=30,random_state=SEED)}
scores = {}
for name, model in models.items():
    model.fit(train[features], train.stockout_rate)
    scores[name] = np.sqrt(np.mean((valid.stockout_rate-model.predict(valid[features]))**2))
chosen = min(scores, key=scores.get)
development = data.query('week <= 13')
model = models[chosen].fit(development[features], development.stockout_rate)
worked_rmse = np.sqrt(np.mean((test.stockout_rate-model.predict(test[features]))**2))
assert np.isclose(worked_rmse, lesson_result(6)['rmse'])

The code runs after the shared setup in the notebook. The downloadable script includes that setup and runs on its own.

Read the model and uncertainty

The mean baseline is the development-period mean outcome. Final RMSE pools all squared errors before taking a square root. The watchlist is ordered by forecast, not by observed target-week outcome.

Change one analytical choice

Try changing the tree depth using only the validation period. Record the decision before looking at the final score. For later deployment after alerts begin, create a new evaluation period for the changed operating process.

How this case is generated

The shared world contains 150 stores followed for 32 weeks. Delivery time, location, demand, promotions, store differences, and a common time pattern generate the probability of a stockout. Each store-week contains 140 product-days. The generator draws their availability and records both policy paths using the same underlying draws.

The expected alert reduction varies with delivery time and location. Offers are randomized only within the 50-store pilot cohort. Voluntary adoption uses measured starting conditions in a separate cohort. The final cohort starts a selected rollout in week 25. These are distinct studies inside the same business history.

Inspect the numerical mechanism

p0 = 0.055 + 0.014 × lead + 0.0005 × (demand − 100) + 0.018 × urban + 0.003 × (lead − 3) × urban + 0.020 × promotion + store effect + 0.006 × sin(week / 4)

Expected reduction = 0.006 + 0.008 × lead + 0.004 × urban; p1 = p0 − reduction

The probabilities are converted to counts by comparing 140 uniform draws with p0 or p1. Cost is 6 CU per stockout product-day plus 20 CU per week when alerts are offered. These costs are the stated management accounting scenario. The complete assignment rules, random streams, and calculations are in the shared source.

Read the shared generator and analysis source

Compare with the known answer

Future demand and shelf availability contain new random variation. The generator stores that variation, but the five forecast inputs expose only information available at the weekly decision time.
